A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoDex, with the same dataset, benchmark definitions, and core experiments. All 19 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, references, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original policy evaluations, prediction-horizon and goal-conditioning experiments, and data/model scaling results in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds OOD-task evaluations and an EncDec+FM prediction-horizon study in Appendix A.1.

M1.justification: The 48-dimensional action representation, trajectory-prediction and inverse-dynamics procedures, architectures, and policy representations are unchanged. The added experiments reuse Dec+BC and EncDec+FM; explicitly naming ARKit does not establish a collection-method change.

E1.justification: v3 newly evaluates six tasks as OOD scenarios, including Jigsaw Puzzle, Knit Scarf, and Stamp Paper (Table 5). Their task labels already appear in v2's inventory; this extends evaluation coverage without establishing an expansion of the underlying dataset.

E2.justification: The main six-policy comparison in Table 2 is unchanged. However, the prediction-horizon study expands from Dec+BC alone in Table 3 to also evaluating EncDec+FM in Table 6, a method already present elsewhere in v2.

E3.justification: v3 adds testing on the separate OOD extra data and EncDec+FM experiments at one- and three-second horizons using the existing K=1,5,10 settings. Original training budgets and metrics remain unchanged. The new statement about randomly sampling 1% of each task clarifies the existing split rather than establishing that it changed.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a targeted six-task OOD generalization analysis and extends the existing horizon sensitivity analysis to EncDec+FM. The original goal-conditioning, dataset-size, model-size, and Dec+BC horizon analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-training run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Best-of-K trajectory sampling is unchanged, and the new tables follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and Figure 5 retain their results. New Table 5 reports Dec+BC OOD average/final distances ranging from 0.047/0.065 m for Jigsaw Puzzle to 0.099/0.162 m for Stamp Paper. Table 6 adds EncDec+FM horizon results: K=10 average distance is 0.026, 0.038, and 0.047 m at one, two, and three seconds, respectively; the two-second row is retained from Table 2.

T1.justification: The action definition, benchmark estimator equations, task-type definitions, and SE(3) annotation specification are unchanged. Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the dataset-release and trajectory-prediction benchmark contributions. The 829-hour, 194-task dataset and its claimed scale and diversity are unchanged; revised application examples do not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new OOD results as supporting generalization to tasks sufficiently similar to training tasks. It removes v2's hypothetical zero-shot deployment argument for a robot matching human appearance and dynamics. Existing scene-diversity and tracking-error limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies per-task random test sampling but removes v2's Dataset Access appendix, including the 725/7/97-hour partition breakdown, archive/download instructions, loading-code disclosure, and CC-by-NC-ND licensing statement. The abstract's repository link and detailed training settings remain; the PDFs establish a documentation change, not withdrawal of access.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to MEgoHand and TASTE-Rob. It removes the explicit statement that Humanoid Policy ~ Human Policy previewed EgoDex using a 3% subset, while retaining citations to that work elsewhere. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose corrections, changes illustrative application examples, removes the separate Overview heading, and reorganizes the appendix around Additional Experiments while dropping Dataset Access. Citations switch to author-year format; most prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5 and 6 and adopts ICLR title, heading, and running-header formatting. Table 4 and appendix figures move with the reflow. Figures 1–7 and the original table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.1 provides useful additional evidence about unseen-task generalization and confirms the horizon trend for EncDec+FM, while Section 5 clarifies the original test split. These limited gains are partly offset by removing dataset partition, download, and licensing documentation. With the repository link, training details, and core results retained, the net improvement is modest.
